subtitle: Picture chore chart for kids
promotionalText: Kids tap a picture when a chore is done. Stars or coins fill their jar and buy rewards your family picks.
description: The Job Jar! is a picture chore chart for kids about 4 to 8, including kids who can't read yet.

Each child taps their own picture, then taps a chore when it's done. Every chore has a big picture and can be read out loud. Finished chores earn stars, and stars buy rewards your family chooses, like extra story time or an ice cream trip.
FOR KIDS
• Big pictures, big buttons, cheerful sounds
• Their own picture or photo, and their own jar
• A week chart that shows what they did each day
FOR GROWN-UPS
• A 4-number PIN keeps settings and rewards for grown-ups
• Check each chore before the stars go in the jar
• Choose which days and which kids each chore is for
• Pay in stars, or in real coins your child can count: pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters
• Special days such as birthdays, when chores pay double or triple
• Special chores that show up only for a few days
• Matching: when Grandma or Granddad offers to match what a child earns, the app adds their share and keeps count
• History of everything earned and spent
• Backup to a file
A KID'S OWN DEVICE
A child's iPad or iPhone can be linked to a grown-up's device with a 6-number code. It shows only that child's chart and stays in step over your home Wi-Fi.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No accounts, no ads, no tracking. Everything stays on your devices. Nothing is sent over the internet.
reviewNotes: SCREEN RECORDING (physical device, current iOS, starting from launching the app): PASTE-LINK-HERE

PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE: The Job Jar! is a picture chore chart for families with young children (about ages 4 to 8), including children who cannot read yet. Problem it solves: paper chore charts get lost and need a grown-up to keep score. Here a child taps a picture when a chore is done, a grown-up confirms it, and the stars (or coins) earned buy rewards the family has chosen. Parents set it up; children use the simple picture screens.

HOW TO SET UP AND USE THE MAIN FEATURES (no account, no login, no sample files needed):
1. Launch the app. Tap "Let's start" and choose any 4-number grown-up PIN (enter it twice), or tap "Skip the PIN for now".
2. Add a kid: type a name, pick a picture, tap Save. Tap Done.
3. On the home screen tap the kid. Tap any chore picture: it turns yellow with an hourglass, waiting for a grown-up.
4. Tap the house button, then Grown-ups, and enter the PIN. On the Check tab tap the green button to OK the chore. The stars go into the kid's jar.
5. Tap Done, tap the kid, then Prizes to see rewards and the "Get it!" button once there are enough stars. "My week" shows the week chart.
6. Grown-ups > Chores and Rewards: add or edit chores and rewards. Grown-ups > Specials: special days (chores pay double), short-time chores, and matching (a grandparent adds a share of what a child earns; this is only a tally inside the app, no payment happens). Grown-ups > Settings: "Pay in money instead of stars" shows the same totals as coins. This is pretend bookkeeping for a family allowance; the app handles no real money and has no purchases.

OPTIONAL SECOND DEVICE: a child's own iPhone or iPad can show just that child's chart. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi. On the grown-up's device: Grown-ups > Devices > Link a kid's device, pick the kid, and a 6-number code appears. On the other device, at first launch tap "This is a kid's device" and type the code. The local network permission is used only for this. The app is fully usable on one device without it.

EXTERNAL SERVICES: none. No server, no accounts or authentication, no analytics, no advertising, no payment processor, no AI service, no third-party SDKs. The app makes no internet connections; all data is stored on the device. Linking uses Apple's MultipeerConnectivity between the family's own devices.
REGIONS: the app works the same in every region. It is in English. Money mode shows US coins (pennies to dollar coins).

REGULATED INDUSTRY / THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL: not applicable. The app is not in a regulated industry and contains no third-party content. All text and artwork were made for the app; pictures of chores are standard system emoji.
ACCOUNTS, USER-GENERATED CONTENT, PAID CONTENT: none. There is no account creation, nothing is shared with other users, and there are no paid features or in-app purchases.
